574-gw-and-counting-indias-wind-fleet.text:
- Claim in post: "India's cumulative installed wind capacity reached 57,443.39 MW by the end of June 2026, per Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) data."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **Newer cumulative figures:** MNRE monthly data, as reported, put cumulative wind capacity at about 58.52 GW on 31 Aug 2026 and 59.20 GW on 30 Sep 2026.
  - **Pace:** 680.75 MW was added in September. H1 FY2026-27 additions total 3,106.23 MW.
  - **Outlook:** an MNRE Joint Secretary said India is on track for 7.5–8 GW of additions in 2026-27.
  - **The post's point still holds:** 59.2 GW is about 8.5% of NIWE's 695.5 GW (120m), so "barely 8 per cent" is unchanged.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.energetica-india.net/news/india-adds-3-69-gw-re-capacity-in-september-2026-total-addition-in-fy27-reaches-24-56-gw
  - https://www.energetica-india.net/news/india-targets-up-to-8-gw-wind-capacity-addition-in-fy27
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. MNRE's monthly data, as reported by trade press, put India's cumulative wind capacity at about 59.2 GW on 30 September 2026, up from the 57.4 GW (June 2026) used below. That is still roughly 8.5% of NIWE's 120m-hub-height potential. State-wise figures below have not been refreshed."
- Confidence: two summaries agree on 59.20 GW, one of them citing PIB. The PIB/MNRE primary was not opened. The offshore item ("a revised tender schedule is expected in the second half of 2026") was also checked. Its window has not closed, and no 2026 tender issue or award was confirmed: one summary described a 7.2 GW Tamil Nadu seabed-lease notice dated mid-2026, but another said those pages repost a 2023 notice. Not flagged; recheck after December 2026.

cpi-wpi-trends-mospi-bulletin.text:
- Claim in post: "Headline WPI inflation was 9.87% in June 2026 (index 110.2, base 2022-23), with Fuel & Power at 27.41%."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **Three newer monthly prints exist.** The Ministry of Commerce and Industry released provisional September 2026 WPI on 14 Oct 2026. Headline inflation was 11.39%, up from 9.92% in August. The index rose to 112.5 from 110.8.
  - **Components, September 2026:** Fuel & Power 25.85% (August 22.93%), Primary Articles 8.67%, Manufactured Products 9.76%.
  - **July 2026 final:** index unchanged at 110.0, inflation 9.78%.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/business/3992075-wpi-inflation-climbs-to-1139-in-september-from-992-in-august
  - https://www.psuconnect.in/news/wpi-inflation-rises-to-11-39-in-september-2026
  - https://www.deccanherald.com/business/wholesale-inflation-surges-to-1139-in-september-4183260
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. Newer WPI releases have come out since this bulletin. Per press coverage of the Office of the Economic Adviser's 14 October 2026 release, headline WPI inflation was 11.39% in September 2026 (provisional), up from 9.92% in August, with Fuel & Power at 25.85%. The 'WPI breaks a year of calm' reading still holds; the rate has risen further since June."
- Confidence: several wire-based summaries agree on 11.39%, 9.92% and 25.85%. The primary eaindustry.nic.in release was not opened. The September figures are provisional.

fipis-biggest-ask-is-getting-natural.text:
- Claim in post: "As of this piece's research, it still hasn't happened, and in 2026 the GST Council instead raised tax on exploration, mining and drilling services from 12% to 18% — moving the opposite direction from what FIPI has asked for." The same year appears in "If anything, 2026 moved in the opposite direction from what FIPI wants — the GST Council raised the tax rate on exploration, mining and drilling services from 12% to 18%". The closing chart is labelled "Rate before 2026" / "Rate after 2026".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The rate change happened in 2025, not 2026.** The post itself said the change should be re-confirmed. PTI reports dated 4 Sep 2025 say services relating to exploration, mining or drilling of petroleum crude or natural gas, and their support services, moved from 12% to 18% with ITC, effective 22 September 2025. That was part of the September 2025 GST rate rationalisation.
  - **Gas is still outside GST.** No 2026 GST Council decision bringing natural gas under GST was found, so "still hasn't happened" holds.
  - **One 2026 recommendation was found.** A single summary (taxo.online, 17 Apr 2026) reported a government committee report published by PNGRB recommending GST inclusion for gas. That is unverified.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.outlookbusiness.com/economy-and-policy/gst-on-oil-and-gas-exploration-hiked-to-18
  - https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/business/2025/09/04/dcm48-biz-gst-oil.html
  - https://www.etvbharat.com/en/!business/gst-on-oil-and-gas-exploration-hiked-enn25090403864
  - https://taxo.online/?p=547365
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. Correction: the GST rate on exploration, mining and drilling services for crude oil and natural gas rose from 12% to 18% with effect from 22 September 2025, as part of the September 2025 GST rate changes (per PTI reports of 4 September 2025), not in 2026. The point stands: natural gas itself remains outside GST, and no GST Council decision to include it was found as of October 2026."
- Confidence: several PTI-wire summaries agree on the rate, the ITC and the 22 September effective date. The year comes from the wire date (2025-09-04). The GST Council notification text was not opened. The April 2026 committee item is single-source and unverified, so it is not in the suggested wording.

if-india-paid-brics-in-rupees-scenario.text:
- Claim in post: "It is on the 2026 summit agenda."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The summit has happened.** The 18th BRICS summit was held in New Delhi on 12–13 September 2026. The "New Delhi Declaration 2026" was adopted unanimously on the opening day.
  - **What the declaration says, per summaries:** it backs expanding trade and investment settlement in local currencies and cross-border payments that are "fast, low-cost, accessible, and transparent". It also backs interoperable national payment systems through the BRICS Payment Task Force, and New Development Bank lending in local currencies. It creates no common currency.
  - **CBDCs not confirmed:** no summary confirmed that the RBI's proposal to link CBDCs appears in the declaration.
  - Seen: summaries only. Several are exam-prep or commercial blogs.
  - https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3367315/under-trumps-shadow-brics-takes-step-towards-de-dollarisation
  - https://visionias.in/current-affairs/news-today/2026-09-14/international-relations/brics-nations-have-unanimously-adopted-the-new-delhi-declaration-in-18th-brics-summit-2026
  - https://organiser.org/2026/09/01/378102/bharat/brics-new-delhi-summit-2026-india-to-push-digital-currencies-for-uninterrupted-cheaper-cross-border-payments/
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. The 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi (12–13 September 2026) adopted the New Delhi Declaration. As reported, it endorses local-currency settlement and interoperable payment systems through the BRICS Payment Task Force, with no common currency. This blog has not confirmed whether the RBI's CBDC-linking proposal appears in the final text. On either reading, the declaration addresses payment friction, not the trade-imbalance constraint modelled here."
- Confidence: dates and adoption are consistent across several summaries. The CBDC wording in the declaration is unverified, and the official text was not read.

indias-coal-to-chemicals-menu-ranked-by.text:
- Claim in post: "zero import duty extended to June 2026" (MEG row of the sorting table). The Sources section repeats it: "MEG at ~$550–665/t with zero import duty through June 2026".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026): Search summaries say Notification No. 12/2026-Customs exempted about 40 petrochemicals, MEG among them, from customs duty from 2 April to 30 June 2026. The Finance Ministry then gave a 15-day transition extension to 15 July 2026. After that the waiver lapsed with no further extension, and the normal 7.5% duty was reinstated. The post was published on 26 August 2026, so this was already out of date when it went up. The post's ranking point survives: MEG is still the second most coal-intensive product, and restoring the duty slightly helps import-parity economics rather than hurting them. Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.chemradar.com/en/service/detail/fifyzcvzm1hc
  - https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/?p=1141340
  - https://a2ztaxcorp.net/?p=35157
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]: The temporary customs-duty waiver on MEG (Notification 12/2026-Customs, 2 April–30 June 2026) was extended only to 15 July 2026 and then lapsed. Trade reports say the standard 7.5% duty has applied since. The 'zero import duty' wording in the table is out of date."
- Confidence: Medium. Three outlets agree on the lapse on 15 July and the 7.5% reinstatement, but the gazette was not seen. No later re-exemption was found in results running to mid-July. A separate proposed MEG anti-dumping duty (DGTR) appeared in results but its status was not verified.

indias-lng-trucks-grew-75-in-2025-about.text:
- Claim in post: "industry sources describe the Government of India as offering no transport-sector incentive for LNG trucks at all, leaving adoption to run on fuel-cost economics alone." The post also says "state-run refiners paused expansion plans in 2026."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **A draft policy was reported in June 2026, before this post (14 Sep 2026).** India Sea Trade News reported a draft Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas proposal to move about a third of long-haul heavy trucks to LNG over 5–7 years. It would allocate domestic gas for an initial three years.
  - **It also reported an instruction to the state-run oil companies** to set up 49 LNG dispensing stations. That sits uneasily with the post's "paused" framing.
  - **Further reports:** the same outlet reported a PNGRB view that LNG would lead long-haul trucking after 2030. One summary mentioned a government review of an incentive programme for cleaner commercial vehicles worth over $1 billion, without naming LNG.
  - **None of this was found to be finalised.** No incentive in force was found, so the post's "no incentive" remains literally true.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://indiaseatradenews.com/government-aims-to-power-33-of-trucks-on-lng-by-2030/
  - https://indiaseatradenews.com/lng-poised-to-lead-long-haul-trucking-in-india-after-2030-pngrb/
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. No LNG-truck incentive is in force, but the policy picture has moved. Trade press reported in mid-2026 a draft oil-ministry plan to shift about a third of long-haul trucks to LNG, with domestic gas allocated for an initial period. The same reports say state oil companies were directed to set up 49 LNG dispensing stations. We have not seen the draft finalised."
- Confidence: low. This is a single outlet, and the search tool flagged date inconsistencies on that site, so the June 2026 dating is unverified. Whether the 49-station instruction came before or after the reported "pause" is also unverified. Check against an MoPNG or PIB source before posting.

indias-semaglutide-patent-cliff-26.text:
- Claim in post: "The same semaglutide composition patent is scheduled to lapse in several other large markets later in 2026 and into 2027 — including China, Brazil, Turkey and South Africa — and Indian manufacturers with domestic launch experience already behind them are positioned to move fastest into those markets too."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **For most of the named markets the compound patent had already lapsed when the post went up (16 Sep 2026).**
    - Industry and IP-firm summaries say the foundational semaglutide patent expired in China, Brazil and India around 20 March 2026 (Abel + Imray; Reddie & Grose; STAT).
    - Abel + Imray also says compound protection has ended in South Africa.
    - Canadian regulatory exclusivity ended in January 2026, with nine generic filings under review at Health Canada (Pearce IP).
    - Turkey is described only as "expired or expiring soon".
  - **Indian exporters:** Dr. Reddy's has said it will export to Canada, Turkey and Brazil.
  - Secondary patents may still complicate entry, and Brazil requires extra impurity and immunogenicity testing.
  - No confirmed generic launch dates in those markets were found.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.abelimray.com/resources/newsletters/ozempic-patent-expiry-have-the-scales-finally-tipped
  - https://www.pearceip.law/?p=83523
  - https://www.reddie.co.uk/2026/02/09/changes-in-the-ozempic-patent-landscape/
  - https://www.iqvia.com/locations/emea/blogs/2026/04/your-questions-answered-off-patent-semaglutide-in-2026
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. Correction to the export section: according to IP-firm and industry summaries, the core semaglutide compound patent lapsed in China and Brazil at about the same time as in India (March 2026), compound protection has also ended in South Africa, and Canadian exclusivity ended in January 2026. Generic entry in those markets depends on regulatory approvals and any secondary patents rather than on a later expiry date."
- Confidence: several secondary IP and industry sources agree on China and Brazil in March 2026. South Africa and Turkey rest on fewer sources and are less certain. No national patent registers were checked. Severity is MEDIUM because the export opportunity still holds, but the timing is wrong.

inflation-trends-globally-what-five.text:
- Claim in post: "The BLS’s CPI-U ran 3.5% over the twelve months to June 2026 — the most recent official print available at the time of writing, with the July release due 12 August 2026." Later the post says that if the July easing reported by the PMI holds, "the 2026 producer spike will have been a two-quarter event rather than a new cycle — and the July and August official prints are the test."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **US CPI:** the September 2026 CPI, released 14 Oct 2026, put 12-month CPI-U at 3.7%. September prices rose 0.6% seasonally adjusted, and gasoline rose 9.1% in the month, more than half of the monthly increase. A third-party tracker puts August at 3.4%.
  - **US PPI:** the BLS reported final-demand PPI up 5.4% over the 12 months to August 2026, with energy up 24.4% year on year. That is a different measure from the All Commodities PPI (PPIACO) the post uses (+10.1% in June), so the two cannot be compared directly. The September PPI (due 15 Oct) was not found.
  - **The test the post set has an answer.** On this reviewer's reading, the official prints since June do not show the producer spike fading as a "two-quarter event". Energy-led pressure persisted in August, and US consumer inflation was higher in September than in June. This is inference and is not stated by any source.
  - Seen: summaries only (the BLS PPI page appeared only as a search-result summary).
  - https://static.poder360.com.br/uploads/2026/10/httpswww.bls_.govnews.releasepdfcpi.pdf
  - https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2026/producer-price-index-up-5-4-percent-for-the-12-months-ended-august-2026.htm
  - https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_09102026.htm
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. Newer official US prints are now out. CPI-U rose 3.7% in the twelve months to September 2026 (BLS, 14 October), and final-demand PPI rose 5.4% in the twelve months to August, with energy up 24.4%. Final-demand PPI is a different measure from the All Commodities index used in Exhibits 4 and 5. On these figures the producer-price rise had not faded by late summer."
- Confidence: the September CPI figure comes from a copy of the BLS release seen as a summary, and the August PPI from BLS pages seen as summaries. The August CPI (3.4%) rests on a single third-party source and is unverified. The "test" reading is the reviewer's own inference. The post's five-year comparison is unaffected.

scan-bottle-deliver-what-ppacs-numbers.text:
- Claim in post: "PPAC's Q1 FY2026-27 report does not state a cause for the 15.6% year-on-year de-growth in April-June 2026 domestic LPG sales, and this piece does not speculate on one." Earlier the post says "a high year-ago base, price or subsidy timing, or a one-quarter demand dip could each explain it".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The fall was not limited to one quarter.**
    - PPAC preliminary data put India's LPG consumption in September 2026 at 2,636 TMT, down 9.15% from 2,902 TMT in September 2025.
    - April–September 2026 was 13,797 TMT, down 14.93% from 16,218 TMT.
    - Earlier reports put April–August domestic consumption down 15.9% at 11.3 million tonnes.
    - One report says August was a six-month high.
  - **Press coverage now gives causes:**
    - continued disruption to supplies through the Strait of Hormuz linked to the conflict involving Iran, Israel and the US;
    - households and industry shifting to piped natural gas, which ThePrint says the government has been pushing.
  - These are national consumption figures from PPAC's monthly releases. They are not the PSU OMC sales series in the LPG Profile Report, so the two are not strictly comparable.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.uniindia.com/business-economy/energy-fuel-demand-sept/200207
  - https://www.constructionworld.in/energy-infrastructure/oil-and-gas/lpg-consumption-falls-9.15-per-cent-in-september/98271
  - https://theprint.in/economy/lpg-consumption-falls-16-as-govt-steps-up-piped-gas-push-amid-energy-supply-disruptions/3032965/
  - https://www.etvbharat.com/amp/en/business/india-lpg-consumption-slides-13-per-cent-amid-west-asia-conflict-enn26041901402

PPAC's preliminary monthly data, as reported in the press, show India's LPG consumption down 14.93% year on year in April–September 2026 and 9.15% in September alone. Press coverage attributes the fall to supply disruption through the Strait of Hormuz and a shift to piped gas. PPAC itself has not been checked for a stated cause. These consumption figures are a different series from the PSU OMC sales in the LPG Profile Report."

tamil-nadus-water-infrastructure-runs.text:
- Claim in post: "The Cooum and Adyar river rejuvenation that made this year's state budget headlines has no dedicated allocation broken out yet — it's a named priority inside a ₹29,863 crore departmental outlay, with feasibility studies and global tenders still pending." Under "What to watch": "Whether the Cooum-Adyar feasibility study produces an actual budget line in a future state budget".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **Central funding was approved before the post went up (25 Aug 2026).** Swarajya reported on 11 June 2026, citing the Times of India, that the Union government gave in-principle approval for Rs 7,500 crore under the Urban Challenge Fund for the Cooum, Adyar and Buckingham Canal revival. This is the first phase of the Chief Minister's Integrated Urban Transformation Mission. Tamil Nadu is reportedly eligible to seek up to Rs 30,000 crore from the fund.
  - **The DPR is being prepared.** Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay later reviewed DPR preparation for the Cooum. A 3-km stretch is being examined for a concept plan and demonstration project, and the work is to be phased. No report says the global tenders have been floated.
  - **The budget figure is confirmed.** The Rs 29,863 crore MAWS outlay is confirmed as the TVK government's maiden budget, up from Rs 26,678 crore.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://swarajyamag.com/amp/story/news-brief/centre-approves-rs-7500-crore-for-cooum-adyar-and-buckingham-canal-revival-under-tamil-nadu-urban-mission
  - https://theprint.in/india/cm-vijay-reviews-progress-on-comprehensive-cooum-river-restoration-project/3050135/
  - https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/tamil-nadu/cm-vijay-reviews-preparation-of-dpr-for-cooum-restoration-1989816
  - https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/cooum-revival-tn-moves-towards-global-tender-phased-riverfront-development
  - https://newstodaynet.com/2026/08/06/cooum-adyar-rejuvenation-tops-maws-outlay/
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. Although the state budget does not itemise Cooum–Adyar spending, a dedicated figure does exist. The Union government reportedly gave in-principle approval in June 2026 for Rs 7,500 crore under the Urban Challenge Fund for the Cooum, Adyar and Buckingham Canal revival, as a first phase. Since then the Chief Minister has reviewed preparation of the Cooum DPR, which is to be phased. No report found says global tenders have been issued. The Rs 7,500 crore figure rests on one press report and is in-principle only."
- Confidence: the Rs 7,500 crore approval comes from a single outlet (Swarajya, citing TOI) and is unverified against a government release. The date of the CM's DPR review was not established. The tender status is inferred from the absence of reports. This predates the post and is an omission of a newer status. The post's point, that no figure reconciles and spending is not itemised, largely survives.

the-currency-rupee-trends-piece-left.text:
- Claim in post: "the same \"Raising Green Debt Globally\" piece already flags BoJ rate hikes (to 1.00% by June 2026, the highest since 1995) as the live risk that could reverse yen weakness and turn future unhedged yen debt costlier, not cheaper, in rupee terms."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The BoJ has raised again since publication (14 Aug 2026).** On 18 September 2026 it raised its policy rate by 0.25 points to 1.25%, on a 7–2 vote. Reports call this the highest since April 1995.
  - **More hikes are signalled.** Commentary reads the statement as pointing to further increases. The next meeting is 29–30 October.
  - **Market reaction:** Babypips reports that the yen weakened rather than strengthened on the day.
  - **The blog already uses the new rate elsewhere.** The companion post which-ecb-currencies-are-actually carries the 1.25% rate in its 7 Oct 2026 update note.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.nippon.com/en/news/yjj2026091800484/
  - https://investinglive.com/central-banks/bank-of-japan-boj-raises-policy-rate-by-25bp-as-expected/
  - https://www.babypips.com/news/headline-boj-rate-hike-september-2026-yen-falls-dovish-ueda
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. Since publication, the Bank of Japan raised its policy rate again, to 1.25% on 18 September 2026 (per Jiji Press and other reports), the highest since 1995, and signalled further increases. The live risk described here has therefore grown, though the yen weakened rather than strengthened on the day of the hike."
- Confidence: Jiji (via Nippon.com), InvestingLive and Babypips agree on 1.25% and the 18 Sep date. The yen's direction on the day comes from Babypips alone.

the-rbi-has-put-bonds-and-rupees-on-one.text:
- Claim in post: "Retail e-rupee circulation, by contrast, was only ₹1,016 crore in March 2025: the RBI’s digital-currency effort has moved decisively from shoppers to markets." The sources note attributes this to "press reports of the RBI Annual Report 2025–26 (May 2026)".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **A newer, lower figure is reported.** Secondary sources attribute ₹771.7 crore of retail e-rupee in circulation on 31 March 2026 to the RBI Annual Report 2025-26, down about 24% from ₹1,016.5 crore a year earlier.
  - **The post's figure comes from the previous year's report.** Deccan Herald's coverage of the earlier annual report gave ₹1,016 crore for end-March 2025.
  - **The newer figure supports the post's point** that the retail e-rupee is shrinking in relevance.
  - **The primary table was not reachable.** An RBI Handbook table (Table 152, dated 31 Jul 2026) appeared in the results, but its figures were cut off.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.legacyias.com/what-do-you-mean-by-digital-rupee-explain-the-working-and-progress-of-indias-central-bank-digital-currency-cbdc/
  - https://www.legacyias.com/?p=182572
  - https://ecorpit.com/programmable-digital-rupee-cbdc-fintech-builder-guide-2026/
  - https://www.deccanherald.com/business/e-rupee-in-circulation-grows-to-rs-1k-cr-rbi-exploring-cross-border-cbdc-pilots-3562394
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. The ₹1,016 crore figure is for March 2025. Secondary reports citing the RBI Annual Report 2025-26 put retail e-rupee circulation at about ₹772 crore on 31 March 2026, a fall of roughly a quarter, which if anything strengthens the point that the RBI's digital-currency effort has moved from shoppers to markets."
- Confidence: low. The ₹771.7 crore figure comes from a civil-services coaching site and a fintech guide, both unverified against the RBI's own text. Confirm against the RBI Annual Report 2025-26 or Handbook Table 152 before posting.

under-corsias-own-numbers-corn-ethanol.text:
- Claim in post: "Set indicative SAF targets: 1% in 2027, 2% in 2028, initially for international flights; 5% by 2030 was added later" and "India has no domestic-flight SAF mandate notified at all, and no SAF-specific national policy — SAF is not integrated into the National Policy on Biofuels 2018, entering only implicitly through that policy's \"drop-in fuels\" definition"
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026): Sources describe the status differently. An S&P Global report dated 30 July 2026 is headlined "India mandates 1% sustainable aviation fuel blend from January 2027". In a 9 July 2026 S&P report, an Indian Oil official describes domestic blending mandates of 1% from 2027 and 2% from 2028. Other summaries still call the targets "indicative" and international-only, and say no domestic targets have been specified. No official notification of a domestic mandate was found. The post was published on 23 September, after the S&P report, but still describes the targets only as "indicative". The post's main finding about corn ethanol and CORSIA defaults is not affected. Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/agriculture/073026-india-mandates-1-sustainable-aviation-fuel-blend-from-january-2027
  - https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/agriculture/070926-ioc-traces-india-saf-journey-with-blending-mandate-flags-feedstock-sustainability-as-core-challenge
  - https://biofuelsdigest.com/india-to-mandate-1-saf-blending-for-2027-reaching-5-in-2030/
- Suggested wording: "Updated 18 October 2026. Some trade reports from July 2026, including S&P Global, describe the 1% figure for 2027 as a mandate rather than an indicative target, and one Indian Oil official spoke of domestic mandates of 1% from 2027 and 2% from 2028. This blog has not found an official notification of a domestic-flight mandate, and other reports still describe the targets as indicative and for international flights."
- Confidence: Sources conflict, and the legal status is unverified. A careful note is warranted, not a correction.

where-indias-gigawatt-data-centre-bets.text:
- Claim in post: The project table row for "Google (with Adani)" reads "$15bn cloud-region alliance with Adani; separate $15bn Visakhapatnam project" with status "First 80 MW site (Adani JV) due mid-2026"
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026): Two searches found no report of an 80 MW Google–Adani site, commissioned or due. The Google–AdaniConneX partnership in the summaries (announced 14 Oct 2025) is the Visakhapatnam AI hub itself: about $15 billion over 2026-2030, groundbreaking reported for 28 April 2026, and about 1 GW expected to be operational by July 2028. A separate deal for Google to lease an AdaniConneX facility in Noida was also reported. So the mid-2026 date has passed with no outcome found. The table may also count the same $15 billion twice. Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/googles-1-35-lakh-crore-ai-data-centre-in-visakhapatnam/print_manually
